## Breaking change
Entity IDs will change due to this PR. However all Entities will be migrated to the new format.
The Device ID will not be migrated.

## Proposed change
Support arbitrary numbers of devices.
Before this change the integration was limited to showing the first device only. With increasing complexity of heating systems this limitation turned out to be a major problem for users.

This required new unique ids to be generated for both: entities and devices.
Devices are not migrated since I could not find a way to do this in Home Assistant. This leads to a stale device when the user updates. **Any pointers on how to fix that would be great**

At the same time this change introduces a new type of tests which can use API dumps as jsons as fixture.

An update of the underlying library PyVicare was also necessary:
https://github.com/somm15/PyViCare/compare/2.21.0...2.25.0

issue_context.title: ViCare integraton adding only one of two boilers
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hi,
I currently have two Viessmann Vitodens 100-W gas boilers, which are visible in the ViCare app (Android) and in the ViGuide account (web).
When I add the ViCare integration to HA only one of them is detected and added as a device, even though in the very first screen after installation (when chosing the area where to place the devices) I see two of them with almost the same name (_E3_Vitodens_100_BHC_0421_), with the first one in bold and the second with "_(Viessmann)_" added at the end.
Once I choose the area, only one device is added, with just two entities for controls ("_ViCare Water_" and "_ViCare Heating_") and not sensors. Once I restart HA Core I get the sensors as well, for a total of 24 entities.
Even after reloading the integration, the second boiler is not detected.
I tried deleting the integration and the deleting the _/config/.storage/vicare_token.save_ file, but when re-adding the integration it's the same thing - just one boiler is added.

When I first added the ViCare integration a couple if weeks ago, both boilers were detected, but the second one had all sensors as "_Unavailable_", even after several hours (the sensors for the first boiler had values after 1-2 minutes at most). I thought that maybe I needed to reinstall the integration to get them to work and now only the first boiler is detected.

I checked the available installations at _https://api.viessmann.com/iot/v1/equipment/installations/_ and I see both boilers there, with the proper names and location details.

Thank you.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.2.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Home Assistant OS

This is wrong. On an invalid login it should prompt the user for new credentials.
This should also be combined with the previous flow:
- INIT => show form
- CONFIGURE (invalid credentials) => show form again
- CONFIGURE (valid crendentials) => create entry
You should keep the `vicare_login` patch here.

Hi @epenet and thanks for taking the time to review this!

I'm not sure I got this right:
I replaced vicare_login with fixtures that return MockPyViCare. This is the purpose of that test refactoring: MockPyViCare allows us to use API json dumps instead of the real API.
I would like to use these mocks in all tests to simulate different heating devices and check the behavior of config flow and later sensors entities, etc.

Why should I keep the vicare_login patch? If I don't introduce the mock there won't be much left in the preliminary PR for conflig flow test refactoring ;)
If it's smaller it's easier to review.
You should keep the `vicare_login` patch here.
These are not config flow tests - they seem to be testing a mock. Please remove this file.
The intention was to verify that the rate limit was correctly set but I agree that this not really the straight-forward way to do this
Please remove this - it should not be present in a core PR.

As with config flow, I suggest that you make a separate preliminary PR for the sensor tests.
You can use https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/90500 as a sample which will make your tests more robust, using `SnapshotAssertion`

Once those tests are in, it will make it clearer what it being affected by the multi-device support PR.

Please refactor the config-flow tests as a preliminary PR:
- as you have done, `mock_setup_entry` should be a fixture but it should return `Generator[AsyncMock, None, None]`
- in `test_config_flow.py`, it should be autoused with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_setup_entry")`
- when you want to inject the fixture, the type hint should be `AsyncMock` (not `bool`)
- you should keep the local `config_flow.vicare_login` patches, and not implement new features

Here's the preliminary config_flow test:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/90568

after that one gets approved I'll create a PR for the sensor test
